01-plumas-public-works-followup.subject: Re: Public Records Act request - Plumas County roadside vegetation-control (herbicide) records
01-plumas-public-works-followup.body:
Dear Mr. Thorman and the Public Works team,

I am following up on the Public Records Act request I sent on September 13, 2026 for the Department's roadside vegetation-control (herbicide) records on county-maintained roads and facilities, January 1, 2020 to the present: the application records by date and road, the Pesticide Use Reports filed with the Plumas-Sierra Agricultural Commissioner, any vegetation-management or IPM plan, herbicide contracts or work orders, and public-notification or no-spray records. We received the mailbox's automatic reply but no determination.

Government Code section 7922.535 asks agencies to respond within 10 days with a determination and, where more time is needed, an estimated production date. Could you please let me know the status of this request and when we might expect the records? If it helps, the application log (date, road, product, amount) is our highest priority and we are glad to take that first with the rest to follow. If the County prefers its records portal or a specific form, point me to it and I will resubmit there.

Electronic delivery to this address is preferred. Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,
Taylor Durgan
Plumas Grassroots Collective / SprayMap California
spraymapca@gmail.com - spraymapca.org

07-kings-new-request.subject: California Public Records Act request - pesticide permit holder names (Kings county code 16)
07-kings-new-request.body:
Dear Commissioner Hook,

Under the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code section 7920.000 et seq.), I request copies of the following public records held by your office:

1. The roster of Operator Identification Numbers / Restricted Materials Permit numbers issued by Kings County (county code 16), together with the permittee / operator name (business or individual) and mailing city/ZIP for each, for permits active at any time during 2020-2026.

2. If maintained as such, your "Permits, Sites, and Commodities" export or the equivalent CalAgPermits PERMIT QUERY covering the same period.

The purpose is to attach real operator names to California Pesticide Use Report records, which CDPR publishes only as coded permit numbers. We map this data at https://www.spraymapca.org. We are not requesting confidential application-site detail beyond what is already public in the PUR, only the operator-ID to name correspondence. Your department's public permit map already gives us names for a few hundred Kings County permits; the full roster would let us name the rest, which is most of them.

Preferred format: a machine-readable file (CSV or Excel). A column of operator/permit IDs and a column of names is sufficient. Several counties have provided exactly this as a CalAgPermits "Permits, Sites and Commodities" export, which takes a few minutes to run.

Fee waiver / costs: this request serves the public interest in government transparency; please waive duplication fees if possible. If costs will exceed $25, please contact me first with an estimate.

Please let me know within the 10-day statutory period (Gov. Code section 7922.535) whether the records exist and when they will be produced. If any portion is withheld, please cite the specific exemption.

Thank you,
Taylor Durgan
Plumas Grassroots Collective / SprayMap California
spraymapca@gmail.com - spraymapca.org

09-usfs-r5-foia-pesticide-use-reports-20.subject: FOIA request - Pesticide-Use Proposals (FS-2100-2) and annual pesticide-use reports, all Region 5 national forests, FY2023 to present
09-usfs-r5-foia-pesticide-use-reports-20.body:
To the Region 5 FOIA Service Center,

Under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. section 552, I request electronic copies of the following records for every national forest in the Pacific Southwest Region (Region 5), for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 to the date of your search:

1. All Pesticide-Use Proposals (Form FS-2100-2) approved or implemented, with the active ingredient(s), product name and EPA registration number, target pest, treatment acreage, application method, quantity applied and treatment location (project or unit name, ranger district, and any spatial data held).

2. The annual pesticide-use reports compiled for each forest and the Region 5 rollup under FSM 2150 / FSH 2109.14 (the Forest Service's annual pesticide use reporting), in whatever form they exist: spreadsheets, database exports or the reports as submitted to the Washington Office.

3. FACTS (Forest Service Activity Tracking System) records for chemical vegetation-control and chemical site-preparation or release activities completed in those fiscal years, with the activity polygons or their attributes (activity code, acres, completion date, forest, district) if the export is practical.

Why this is asked: California's Pesticide Use Report does not cover applications made by federal employees on federal land, so the Forest Service's own reporting is the only public record of herbicide use across a fifth of the state. Our public, noncommercial map at https://www.spraymapca.org carries the state data through 2023 and the FACTS records already released to us; the fiscal years above are the gap. This request is Region-wide and separate from our pending Plumas National Forest request 2026-FS-R5-05799-F.

Format: machine-readable exports (CSV, Excel, or shapefile/geodatabase for spatial data) are preferred over PDF. If a records search is easier per forest, a rolling release by forest is welcome.

Fee waiver: I request a waiver of fees under 5 U.S.C. section 552(a)(4)(A)(iii). Disclosure is in the public interest because it will contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government, namely where and how much herbicide the Forest Service applies on public land in California, and the information will be published free of charge on a public map. The request is not for commercial use. If fees are not waived, please notify me before incurring costs above $50.

Please acknowledge the request with a tracking number and, per 5 U.S.C. section 552(a)(6)(A), provide a determination within 20 working days.

Thank you,
Taylor Durgan
Plumas Grassroots Collective / SprayMap California
spraymapca@gmail.com - spraymapca.org

11-reply-dante-gasser-fopw.subject: Re: Community Meeting
11-reply-dante-gasser-fopw.body:
Hi Dante,

Thank you for coming on Tuesday, and for writing. Your feedback is fair and useful, and I would much rather hear it directly than not at all.

You are right that the second half got away from the format we intended. [Taylor: two or three sentences on where the last hour went, and anything that was decided about the next meeting.]

For the next session we want the room built the way you describe: the RCD, Plumas Corp, the Forest Service, UC Cooperative Extension and industry representatives invited in advance and given time on the agenda, a moderator who holds speakers to the topic and the clock, and no one called out who is not in the room to answer. The science briefing stays the anchor.

Would you be willing to meet for coffee in Quincy before then? Friends of Plumas Wilderness knows this forest better than most, and I would value your read on what a productive process looks like. I would also like to add you to the notices list for the meeting series; tell me if you would rather I did not.

Thank you again for the kind words about the map. It exists so that conversations like Tuesday's can start from the same facts.

Best,
Taylor Durgan
Plumas Grassroots Collective / SprayMap California
